title: A moving object keeps a steady straight path until a net force acts
summary: A moving object keeps the same speed in a straight line until a net outside force changes that motion.
body: The second part of Newton's first law, as OpenStax Physics states it, is that a body in motion tends to keep a constant velocity unless a net outside force acts. Constant velocity, the page says, means a straight line at a constant speed. The book notes that this can seem to clash with daily life, because moving things usually slow down. The slowing is a force, not the object deciding to stop. Urone and Hinrichs, 26 March 2020.
